summary: A 1975 tentative schedule from BBN for implementing the new Telnet protocol in the TIP, which had become the top item on its development queue. It lists target dates because TIP changes affect many hosts.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 688 gives BBN's tentative schedule for implementing the new TELNET protocol in the TIP. The milestones cover design, options, an initial option set and final host compatibility work.

questions: what was the tip telnet implementation schedule
which options were planned for the tip
did rfc 688 report completed telnet work
subtitle: A tentative schedule for adding the new TELNET protocol and options to the TIP.

tldr.problem: Implementation of the new TELNET protocol had become the top item on the TIP development queue, and its changes could affect other hosts.
tldr.mechanism: BBN publishes four target milestones, moving from basic design to option design, operation of a basic option set and a stable implementation.
tldr.outcome: The document gives a tentative schedule for work planned during 1975; it does not report whether the milestones were met.

today: The unit records RFC 688's status as Unknown and lists no updates or obsoleting RFCs. It is a tentative 1975 implementation schedule for the TIP.

sections.title: Why the TIP Schedule Was Shared
sections.content:
David Walden says implementation of the new TELNET protocol had become the top priority in the TIP development queue. Since TIP work could affect what other hosts did, BBN shared the schedule it hoped to follow.

The schedule is described as tentative. It gives target dates and planned capabilities rather than reporting completed work.
sections.plainLanguage: Changes to the TIP could affect other hosts, so BBN published its planned work dates. The RFC presents them as targets, not as completed milestones.

sections.title: Design and Option Milestones
sections.content:
By July 18, 1975, the basic design was to be complete and a TIP version with a general option negotiator was to be operational, though it would refuse all options. By mid-September, the design of the options was to be complete, with an operational version containing necessary option support.

These milestones move from basic negotiation capability to the design work needed to support options.
sections.plainLanguage: The first target is a working negotiator that refuses all options. A later target completes the design of the options themselves.

sections.title: The Planned Option Set and Final Version
sections.content:
By mid-November, BBN hoped to have an operational TIP version with Binary Transmission, Echo, Suppress Go-Ahead, Timing Mark and RCTE options. By the end of 1975, the schedule aimed to resolve host problems, make necessary revisions and have a solid TIP version running the TELNET protocol with options.

The RFC gives these as intended milestones and does not include a later progress report.
sections.plainLanguage: The planned option set included Binary Transmission, Echo, Suppress Go-Ahead, Timing Mark and RCTE. The final target was a stable version by the end of 1975, after host issues were addressed.
